_comment: This is the ONLY file you should need to edit. 'paths' tells the suite where your binary lives; 'implemented' tells it which flags your chmod supports so it only runs applicable cases. Everything else has a sensible default. judge_candidate.sh overrides both on a throwaway copy and never writes here.

paths._comment: candidate_bin: your normal (non-instrumented) build. Required for runner.py. For example: agentic_cyber/build/new_chmod
paths._comment2: candidate_asan_bin: an ASan/UBSan-instrumented build. Optional; runner.py --sanitizer uses it. Leave candidate_src empty to bring your own instead of having build_asan.sh compile one.
paths._comment3: candidate_src / cc / cc_flags: only used by build_asan.sh, only if your chmod is a single C source file you want this suite to compile with sanitizers.

_comment4: There is no oracle binary. new_chmod is a bounded utility whose contract comes from the checkpoint prompts, and the goldens are frozen offline and compared byte for byte. No oracle implementation ships with these tests.
_comment5: implemented: flag IDs your binary currently supports. A frozen case only runs if every ID in its own 'flags' list appears here. The list below is a placeholder -- the experiment harness supplies the cumulative checkpoint list at runtime.
